protocol: T4a: attenuator-linearity sweep, radiated (PMR446 handset -> HackRF, LNA32/VGA40, channel 8 / 446.09375 MHz nominal). Fixed setup: handset, HackRF, receive antenna and cable, operator position unchanged between points -- only the attenuator combo (built from 3/20/30 dB units) and, between the two sweeps, the handset's TX power setting. Attenuators are uncertified; their real tolerance is unknown and is not corrected for anywhere in this file. Addendum after two SMA disconnects in the Low sweep: check the receive antenna connector's torque before EVERY point, not just at the start of the sweep -- likely mechanical tension from the cable run, not bad luck.
metric: Per capture: PolyphaseChannelizer (production config, 2 MS/s, 160 ch, decimation 80) on the strongest bin excluding the DC guard and the Nyquist edge guard (same convention as esm446.core.node.EsmNode). mean_dbfs is 10*log10(mean(linear power)) over every post-settle frame (first 50 frames dropped for filter-bank group delay) -- not a mean of dB values. peak_dbfs and min_dbfs are the frame extremes in dB. spread_db = peak - min, the diagnostic for whether PTT was held continuously (or the connector stayed seated) through the whole capture. Window is 10 s except where a point's label says otherwise (the 50-53 dB tail's follow-up used 60 s).
not_yet_resolved: No point exists between 33 dB and 50 dB in either sweep -- the transition out of saturation happens somewhere in that 17 dB gap, and its shape is unknown. Proposed next step: shift the whole curve by lowering handset TX power further or increasing distance, not by buying more attenuators (3/20/30 dB cannot combine to land inside this gap).

The Low sweep's 53 dB point is IMPROVED, NOT RESOLVED: two 60 s follow-up captures (-8.65 and -9.69 dBFS, 1.04 dB apart) narrowed the gap from the original two 10 s captures (-11.52 and -8.68 dBFS, 2.84 dB apart), confirming the slow-drift hypothesis's direction, but 1.04 dB residual disagreement at the highest-attenuation point in the sweep -- exactly where precision matters most, closest to the noise floor -- is not a converged number. Do not treat either 60 s value as the answer. Next step if T4a is resumed: a 120 s window, not another 10 s or 60 s repeat.
No slope or absolute-linearity conclusion is drawn from this data. It documents what was measured, including what did not converge.

points.label: p1_0db
points.reason: script bug: pre-fix active/floor heuristic assumed intermittent PTT and returned mean_active_dbfs=None under continuous PTT (see p1_0db_v2 for the fix)

points.label: p7_50db
points.reason: 11.87 dB intra-capture spread triggered the script's own PTT-gap warning; the user's confirmation message arrived truncated ("50 db, tax"), consistent with an interrupted PTT

points.label: p7_50db_v2
points.reason: protocol violation, not a data problem: launched by the agent before the user's explicit "listo" confirmation for this repeat, so PTT state during the capture cannot be verified either way

points.label: p8_53db
points.reason: 8.78 dB intra-capture spread, well above the ~3-4 dB typical of a clean point; user confirmed PTT was held throughout, so attributed to real signal fading rather than a PTT gap -- repeated for confirmation, and the repeat's tighter spread (1.43 dB) was preferred

points.label: low_p4_23db
points.reason: 6.01 dB intra-capture spread, elevated vs. the ~3-4 dB baseline; retroactively attributed to the receive antenna connector already loosening before it fully disconnected during setup of the next point (30 dB)

points.label: low_p4_23db_v2
points.note: repeat after the receive antenna connector was confirmed reseated "the same way" (operator's words)

points.label: low_p5_30db_attempt_a
points.reason: rejected by the operator before the capture ran: the handset radio was powered off

points.label: low_p5_30db_attempt_b
points.reason: rejected by the operator before the capture ran: the receive antenna connector had fallen off (incident 1 of 2 at this point)

points.label: low_p5_30db_v2
points.reason: reading moved in the wrong direction relative to the (later found to be equally contaminated) first 23 dB attempt; retained as suspect pending confirmation of the antenna reseat, superseded once the connector's mechanical firmness could not be independently guaranteed

points.label: low_p5_30db_v3
points.reason: 110.86 dB intra-capture spread (min -107.43 dBFS, essentially the thermal floor, mid-capture): the receive antenna connector fell a second time during this specific capture, cutting the signal for part of the window

points.label: low_p5_30db_v4
points.note: captured after the operator explicitly confirmed the antenna connector was firm

points.label: low_p6_33db
points.note: no incident reported at this point

points.label: low_p8_53db
points.reason: does not converge with its own repeat (low_p8_53db_v2); no capture-level fault found in either (spreads 6.29 and 3.66 dB, both below the PTT-gap warning threshold and both confirmed PTT-held). Kept as an observed range, not averaged.

points.label: low_p8_53db_v2
points.reason: does not converge with low_p8_53db -- see that entry

points.label: low_p8_53db_60s
points.note: connector torque checked/tightened before this point (protocol addendum); 60 s window per the slow-drift hypothesis (10 s captures showed only 3-6 dB intra-capture spread, ruling out fast fading -- instability was between separate captures, not within one)
points.reason: run under real memory pressure on this machine (7.6 GB RAM): decoding 60 s to a single complex64 array plus the full spectra array approached ~2 GB, drove the system into swap, and the process hung on shutdown after printing this result (killed by an external timeout at exit code 124, but the printed result itself completed normally). 1 overrun recorded, plausibly from the same system lag during capture. Not discarded outright, but flagged: this is the run that motivated the streaming rewrite used for the next point.

points.label: low_p8_53db_60s_v2
points.note: same conditions as low_p8_53db_60s, rerun with a memory-streaming version of the analysis script (chunked file reads and running accumulators instead of one full-capture array) after the previous run's swap/hang. Clean: no lag, no overruns -- but NOT a converged reading by itself. It disagrees with low_p8_53db_60s by 1.04 dB; see not_yet_resolved above. Next step if this point is revisited: 120 s, not another repeat at 60 s.

capture_layer_note: Every capture in this file returned overruns=0 except low_p8_53db_60s (1 overrun, under real memory pressure on the analysis side -- see that entry). No capture ever failed to complete at the hackrf_transfer/USB layer. Every discarded or unresolved point here is a physical (antenna connector), procedural (PTT timing, agent launch timing), analysis-side resource, or propagation (fading) issue, not a repeat of the capture-failure pattern documented in scripts/overnight_survey.py's run_c2/run_c3 circuit breakers.
